note: Practice questions (26) and timed-set questions (15) taken from SAT-Desmos-Strategies.html on 2026-11-12, before any rewording. build_desmos3.py adapts them.

practice.stem: In the parabola $y = 2x^{2} - 7$, what is the $x$-coordinate of the positive $x$-intercept, rounded to the nearest hundredth?
practice.sol:
Given: $y = 2x^{2} - 7$; want the positive root.

Graph and hover the right-hand $x$-intercept: $(1.871,\,0)$. Or: $2x^2 = 7 \Rightarrow x = \sqrt{3.5} \approx 1.87$.

1.87

practice.stem: The graph of $y = -x^{2} + 4x + 6$ has two $x$-intercepts. What is the $x$-coordinate of the one that is positive, rounded to the nearest hundredth?
practice.sol:
Given: $y = -x^{2} + 4x + 6$.

Hover the right-hand intercept: $(5.162,\,0)$. Quadratic formula check: $x = 2 \pm \sqrt{10}$, and $2 + \sqrt{10} \approx 5.16$.

5.16

practice.stem: $$4x - 3y = 10$$ $$x + 2y = 8$$ If $(x,\,y)$ is the solution to the system above, what is the value of $x + y$?
practice.sol:
Given: two lines; want $x + y$ at their intersection.

Graph both; they cross at $(4,\,2)$. So $x + y = 6$. (Read the question twice: it asks for the sum, not $x$.)

6

practice.stem: $$y = -3x + 11$$ $$y = x - 5$$ The solution to the system above is $(x,\,y)$. What is the value of $y$?
practice.sol:
Given: two lines in slope-intercept form; want the $y$-value of the intersection.

Hover the crossing: $(4,\,-1)$. Check: $-3x + 11 = x - 5 \Rightarrow 4x = 16 \Rightarrow x = 4$, $y = -1$.

−1

practice.stem: The function $f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 5$ intersects the $x$-axis at two points. What is the sum of the $x$-coordinates of those points?
practice.sol:
Given: $f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 5$.

The $x$-intercepts read $(1,\,0)$ and $(5,\,0)$, so the sum is $6$. Check: $(x-1)(x-5) = 0$.

6

practice.stem: At what positive value of $x$ does the graph of $f(x) = 2x^{2} - 5x - 3$ cross the $x$-axis?
practice.sol:
Given: $f(x) = 2x^{2} - 5x - 3$; want the positive zero.

Intercepts at $(-0.5,\,0)$ and $(3,\,0)$. Check: $(2x+1)(x-3) = 0$.

3

practice.stem:
How many solutions does the following system have? $$6x - 4y = 10$$ $$3x - 2y = 5$$

  • AZero
  • BExactly one
  • CExactly two
  • DInfinitely many
practice.sol:
Given: two equations in standard form.

Graph both: only one line appears, because the first equation is exactly twice the second. Every point on the line satisfies both.

D, infinitely many

practice.stem:
How many solutions does the following system have? $$2x + 3y = 6$$ $$4x + 6y = 9$$

  • AZero
  • BExactly one
  • CExactly two
  • DInfinitely many
practice.sol:
Given: two equations in standard form.

The graphs are parallel: both have slope $-\tfrac{2}{3}$ but different intercepts ($y=2$ vs. $y=1.5$). Parallel lines never meet.

A, zero

practice.stem: How many times does the circle $(x - 2)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = 9$ intersect the $x$-axis?
practice.sol:
Given: center $(2,\,3)$, radius $3$.

The lowest point is at $y = 3 - 3 = 0$, exactly on the axis. The circle is tangent to the $x$-axis, touching it once at $(2,\,0)$.

1

practice.stem: How many times does the graph of $(x + 2)^{2} + (y - 1)^{2} = 25$ intersect the $x$-axis?
practice.sol:
Given: center $(-2,\,1)$, radius $5$.

The center is only 1 unit above the axis and the radius is 5, so the circle dips well below it and crosses twice, at $x \approx 2.90$ and $x \approx -6.90$.

2

practice.stem: $$h(x) = -(x - 1)(x + 7)$$ For what value of $x$ does $h$ reach its maximum value, and what is that maximum?
practice.sol:
Given: zeros at $x = 1$ and $x = -7$; parabola opens down.

Vertex $x$ is the midpoint of the zeros: $\dfrac{1 + (-7)}{2} = -3$. Then $h(-3) = -(-4)(4) = 16$. Desmos shows the vertex dot at $(-3,\,16)$.

x = −3, maximum 16

practice.stem: What is the minimum value of the function $f(x) = 2x^{2} + 8x - 3$?
practice.sol:
Given: $f(x) = 2x^{2} + 8x - 3$, opening upward.

Hover the vertex: $(-2,\,-11)$. The question asks for the minimum value, which is the $y$-coordinate. Check: $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -2$, $f(-2) = 8 - 16 - 3 = -11$.

−11

practice.stem: $$f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 10$$ The graph of $f$ is translated down 4 units. How many times does the translated graph intersect the $x$-axis?
practice.sol:
Given: $f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 10$; new graph is $f(x) - 4$.

Vertex of $f$: $(3,\,1)$, above the axis, so $f$ has no real zeros. Down 4 puts the vertex at $(3,\,-3)$; an upward parabola with vertex below the axis crosses twice.

2

practice.stem: $$f(x) = -x^{2} + 2x + 3$$ The graph of $f$ is translated up 3 units. What is the maximum value of the translated function?
practice.sol:
Given: $f(x) = -x^{2} + 2x + 3$; new graph is $f(x) + 3$.

Vertex of $f$ reads $(1,\,4)$. Shifting up 3 moves it to $(1,\,7)$, so the new maximum value is $7$.

7

practice.stem: The data set $\{4,\ 4,\ 9,\ 11,\ 15,\ 20,\ 21\}$ has mean $m$ and median $d$. What is $m - d$?
practice.sol:
Given: seven values (already sorted).

mean(...) gives $\dfrac{84}{7} = 12$; median(...) gives the 4th value, $11$.

$$m - d = 12 - 11 = 1$$1

practice.stem: What is the sum of the mean and the median of the data set $\{6,\ 9,\ 10,\ 10,\ 14,\ 17,\ 22,\ 24\}$?
practice.sol:
Given: eight values.

Mean $= \dfrac{112}{8} = 14$. With an even count, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values: $\dfrac{10 + 14}{2} = 12$.

$$14 + 12 = 26$$26

practice.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to $|2x + 3| = 9$?
practice.sol:
Given: $|2x + 3| = 9$.

Graph $y = |2x+3|$ and $y = 9$; intersections at $x = 3$ and $x = -6$.

$$3 + (-6) = -3$$−3

practice.stem: What is the sum of the solutions to $|3x - 4| = 8$? Enter your answer as a fraction or a decimal.
practice.sol:
Given: $|3x - 4| = 8$.

Crossings at $x = 4$ and $x = -\dfrac{4}{3}$ (Desmos shows $-1.333$).

$$4 + \left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = \dfrac{8}{3}$$

Enter 8/3 or 2.666 or 2.667, not 2.67.

8/3

practice.stem: $$y \le 2x - 1$$ $$y \ge -x + 5$$ The point $(3,\,y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities above. What is one possible value of $y$?
practice.sol:
Given: $x = 3$; want $y$ inside both shaded regions.

Along the vertical line $x = 3$, the overlap runs from $y = 2$ up to $y = 5$ (solid boundaries, so both endpoints count).

Check: $y \le 5$ and $y \ge 2$.

any y with 2 ≤ y ≤ 5

practice.stem:
$$y > x + 1$$ $$y < -2x + 10$$ Which of the following points is a solution to the system of inequalities above?

  • A$(1,\,1)$
  • B$(2,\,4)$
  • C$(0,\,12)$
  • D$(4,\,3)$
practice.sol:
Given: four candidate points; want the one in the doubly-shaded region.

Plot the points on top of the inequalities: only $(2,\,4)$ lands in the overlap. Check: $4 > 3$ ✓ and $4 < 6$ ✓. $(0,\,12)$ fails the second inequality, the other two fail the first.

B

practice.stem:
Which of the following is an equation of a line with slope $-2$ and $y$-intercept $6$?

  • A$x + 2y = 6$
  • B$2x - y = 6$
  • C$2x + y = 6$
  • D$y = 2x + 6$
practice.sol:
Given: the line must pass through $(0,\,6)$ and fall 2 for every 1 to the right.

Graph all four. Only $2x + y = 6$ crosses the $y$-axis at 6 and slopes downward. Rewritten: $y = -2x + 6$.

C

practice.stem:
Which of the following is an equation of a line that has an $x$-intercept of $3$ and passes through the point $(6,\,-4)$?

  • A$3x + 4y = 12$
  • B$4x - 3y = 12$
  • C$3x - 4y = 12$
  • D$4x + 3y = 12$
practice.sol:
Given: the line must pass through $(3,\,0)$ and $(6,\,-4)$.

Plot the point $(6,\,-4)$ with the four lines; only $4x + 3y = 12$ goes through it while also hitting $(3,\,0)$. Check: $4(6) + 3(-4) = 12$ ✓. Choice B has the right $x$-intercept but the wrong slope.

D

practice.stem: $$5x - 2y = 7$$ $$10x + ky = 3$$ In the system above, $k$ is a constant. For what value of $k$ does the system have no solutions?
practice.sol:
Given: no solutions means parallel, distinct lines.

Slope of line 1: $\dfrac{5}{2}$. Slope of line 2: $-\dfrac{10}{k}$. Parallel when $-\dfrac{10}{k} = \dfrac{5}{2} \Rightarrow k = -4$. The slider confirms the lines never meet at $k = -4$, and $10x - 4y = 3$ is not a multiple of $5x - 2y = 7$, so they're distinct.

k = −4

practice.stem: $$2x + 5y = 12$$ $$kx + 10y = 24$$ In the system above, $k$ is a constant. For what value of $k$ does the system have infinitely many solutions?
practice.sol:
Given: infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line.

Slide $k$ until the second line sits exactly on top of the first; that happens at $k = 4$. Check: doubling $2x + 5y = 12$ gives $4x + 10y = 24$.

k = 4

practice.stem:
Which equation best approximates the line of best fit for the points $(1, 3)$, $(4, 8)$, $(6, 11)$, and $(10, 18)$?

  • A$y = 1.7x + 1.3$
  • B$y = 1.3x + 1.7$
  • C$y = 2.1x - 0.4$
  • D$y = 0.6x + 4.5$
practice.sol:
Given: four data points; want $y \approx mx + b$.

Table, then y1 ~ m x1 + b: Desmos reports $m \approx 1.661$, $b \approx 1.281$. Closest choice: A. (B swaps the two numbers.)

A

practice.stem:
A line of best fit is drawn through the points $(0, 4)$, $(3, 7)$, $(5, 10)$, and $(8, 12)$. Which of the following best approximates its slope and $y$-intercept?

  • Aslope $\approx 4.1$, intercept $\approx 1.0$
  • Bslope $\approx 1.0$, intercept $\approx 4.1$
  • Cslope $\approx 0.5$, intercept $\approx 4.0$
  • Dslope $\approx 1.5$, intercept $\approx 2.0$
practice.sol:
Given: four data points.

Regression output: $m \approx 1.029$, $b \approx 4.132$. Slope about 1, intercept about 4.1: choice B. Choice A swaps them.

B

timed.title: Ticket sales system
timed.prompt: A movie theater sold a total of 240 tickets to a showing. Adult tickets cost $12 each and child tickets cost $8 each, and the theater collected $2{,}480 from the sale. How many child tickets were sold?
timed.desmos: Let $x$ be adult tickets and $y$ child tickets. Type x + y = 240 and 12x + 8y = 2480; the lines meet at $(140,\,100)$. The question asks for child tickets, the $y$-value: $100$.

timed.title: Ball hits the ground
timed.prompt: A ball is thrown upward from a platform. The height of the ball above the ground, in feet, $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by the function $h(t) = -16t^{2} + 48t + 64$. How many seconds after it is thrown does the ball hit the ground?
timed.desmos: Graph $y = -16x^{2} + 48x + 64$ (use $x$ for $t$). Zoom out until the parabola crosses the $x$-axis on the right; the grey dot reads $(4,\,0)$. The other intercept, $x = -1$, is before the throw and does not count.

timed.title: Mean from a frequency table
timed.prompt: The table shows the number of pets owned by each of 20 households in a survey.
timed.figure:
Number of pets0123
Number of households6842
timed.prompt2: What is the mean number of pets per household for the 20 households?
timed.desmos: Type (0*6 + 1*8 + 2*4 + 3*2)/20 and Desmos shows $1.1$. (Or build a table with the pet counts and frequencies and type total(x1*y1)/total(y1).)
timed.algebra: Total pets $= 0 + 8 + 8 + 6 = 22$ across $20$ households, so the mean is $\dfrac{22}{20} = 1.1$.

timed.title: Gym fee from two bills
timed.prompt: A gym charges members a fixed monthly fee plus a constant charge for each visit. One member who visited 6 times in a month was charged $57, and another member who visited 11 times in the same month was charged $77. What is the fixed monthly fee, in dollars?
timed.desmos: Put the two points $(6,\,57)$ and $(11,\,77)$ in a table and type y1 ~ m x1 + b. Desmos reports $m = 4$ and $b = 33$. The intercept $b$ is the charge with zero visits: the monthly fee.

timed.title: Equation of a circle
timed.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, a circle has center $(-4,\,6)$, and the point $(-4,\,1)$ lies on the circle. Which equation represents the circle?
timed.desmos: Type the point $(-4,6)$, the point $(-4,1)$, and then each answer choice. Only choice A draws a circle centered on the first point that passes through the second.
timed.algebra: The radius is the distance from $(-4,\,6)$ to $(-4,\,1)$, which is $5$, so $r^{2} = 25$. In $(x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}$ the center $(-4,\,6)$ gives $(x + 4)^{2} + (y - 6)^{2}$.

timed.title: Linear function values
timed.prompt: The function $f$ is linear. If $f(2) = 7$ and $f(5) = 16$, what is the value of $f(10)$?
timed.desmos: Enter $(2,\,7)$ and $(5,\,16)$ in a table and run y1 ~ m x1 + b: $m = 3$, $b = 1$. Then type 3(10) + 1, or define $f(x) = 3x + 1$ and type f(10).

timed.title: Car value halves
timed.prompt: A car was purchased for $24{,}000. The value of the car decreases by 15% each year after the purchase. According to this model, what is the least whole number of years after the purchase at which the value of the car will be less than half of the purchase price?
timed.desmos: Graph $y = 24000(0.85)^{x}$ and $y = 12000$ (set the window to $x$ from $0$ to $10$ and $y$ up to $25{,}000$). They cross at $x \approx 4.27$. After 4 years the value is still above half; after 5 whole years it is below.

timed.prompt2: Based on the line of best fit, which of the following is closest to the predicted sales, in dollars, on a day with a high temperature of $30^{\circ}$C?
timed.desmos: Read the five points off the graph, put them in a table, and type y1 ~ m x1 + b: Desmos redraws the same line ($m \approx 12.4$, $b \approx -7.7$). Then type m*30 + b to get $363.9$, closest to $364$. Reading the drawn line at $30$ by eye gives the same answer; Desmos just removes the guesswork.
timed.algebra: The line rises about $12$ dollars per degree (from $240$ at $20^{\circ}$ to about $350$ at $29^{\circ}$). One degree past the last point: $350 + 12 \approx 362$, so $364$ is the closest choice.

timed.title: Equivalent expression
timed.prompt: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $(x + 3)(x - 5) + 2(x - 1)$?
timed.desmos: Graph $y = (x + 3)(x - 5) + 2(x - 1)$, then graph each choice. The choice whose curve lies exactly on top of the first one (only one curve visible) is equivalent: choice A.

timed.title: Minimum deliveries
timed.prompt: A delivery driver is paid $18 per hour plus $4 for each delivery completed. The driver works 7 hours in one day and wants to earn at least $200 that day. What is the minimum number of deliveries the driver must complete?
timed.desmos: Graph $y = 18(7) + 4x$ and $y = 200$. They cross at $x = 18.5$. Deliveries are whole numbers and the pay must reach at least $200$, so round up to $19$.
timed.algebra: $126 + 4d \ge 200 \Rightarrow 4d \ge 74 \Rightarrow d \ge 18.5$. The smallest whole number is $19$. (18 deliveries gives only $198.)

timed.title: Exactly one solution
timed.prompt: The equation $2x^{2} + bx + 8 = 0$, where $b$ is a positive constant, has exactly one solution. What is the value of $b$?
timed.desmos: Graph $y = 2x^{2} + bx + 8$ and add a slider for $b$. Drag $b$ until the parabola just touches the $x$-axis at a single point. That happens at $b = 8$ (and at $b = -8$, which is ruled out because $b$ is positive).
timed.algebra: One solution means the discriminant is zero: $b^{2} - 4(2)(8) = 0 \Rightarrow b^{2} = 64 \Rightarrow b = 8$ since $b > 0$.

timed.title: Yearly percent increase
timed.prompt: The function $A(t) = 300(2)^{t/5}$ models the value, in dollars, of an investment $t$ years after it was made. Which of the following is closest to the percent increase in the value of the investment each year, according to the model?
timed.desmos: Rewrite the growth factor per year: $2^{t/5} = \left(2^{1/5}\right)^{t}$. Type 2^(1/5) and Desmos shows $1.1487$, a yearly increase of about $14.9\%$. (Or graph $A$ and compare $A(1)/A(0)$.)
timed.algebra: Each year multiplies the value by $2^{1/5} \approx 1.149$, which is a $14.9\%$ increase, closest to $15\%$.

timed.title: Circle and line
timed.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x + 4y = 12$ is a circle. How many points do the circle and the line $y = x - 1$ have in common?
timed.desmos: Desmos graphs the circle from the general form as written, no completing the square needed. Add $y = x - 1$: the line cuts through the circle at two grey dots.
timed.algebra: Complete the square: $(x - 3)^{2} + (y + 2)^{2} = 25$, center $(3,\,-2)$, radius $5$. The distance from the center to the line $x - y - 1 = 0$ is $\dfrac{|3 + 2 - 1|}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 2.83 < 5$, so the line crosses the circle twice.

timed.title: Area between graphs
timed.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the graphs of $y = |x - 3| + 1$ and $y = 5$ intersect at two points. What is the area of the triangle formed by those two points and the vertex of the graph of $y = |x - 3| + 1$?
timed.desmos: Graph both. The V has its vertex at $(3,\,1)$ and crosses $y = 5$ at $(-1,\,5)$ and $(7,\,5)$. The base along $y = 5$ is $8$ and the height down to the vertex is $4$: area $\tfrac{1}{2}(8)(4) = 16$.

timed.title: Tangent line, constant k
timed.prompt: $$y = x^{2} + 4x + k$$ $$y = 2x + 1$$ In the given system of equations, $k$ is a constant. The system has exactly one solution. What is the value of $k$?
timed.desmos: Type both equations and add a slider for $k$. Drag $k$ until the line just touches the parabola (one grey dot instead of two or none). That is $k = 2$.
timed.algebra: Set equal: $x^{2} + 4x + k = 2x + 1 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 2x + (k - 1) = 0$. One solution when the discriminant is zero: $4 - 4(k - 1) = 0 \Rightarrow k = 2$.
